title: Influence of rapamycin on safety and healthspan metrics after one year: PEARL trial results | Aging
abstract: **Figure 1.** **Changes in body composition measures in response to rapamycin use.** Females using 10 mg of rapamycin had significant improvements in lean tissue mass at 24 and 48 weeks relative to both placebo (24 week: *md* = 3.60472 (95% CI = 0.0913–7.1182), *p* = 0.043; 48 week: *md* = 6.194 (95% CI = 0.8773–11.5105), *p* = 0.018) and 5mg groups (24 week: *md* = 3.774 (95% CI = 0.3271–7.2212), *p* = 0.028; 48 week: *md* = 5.565 (95% CI = 0.5311–10.5979), *p* = 0.026) (**A**). **Figure 2.** **Changes in self-reported survey scores of quality of life and health.** Females using 10 mg of rapamycin again had significant improvements in self-reported measures of pain at both 24 and 48 weeks (24 weeks: *md* = 6.765 (95% CI = 1.315–12.215), *p* = 0.011; 48 weeks: *md* = 8.071 (95% CI = 3.044–13.098), *p* < 0.001) (**A**).
